thread.title: Nvidia leads Silicon Valley stock rally at end of tumultuous week

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Nvidia leads Silicon Valley stock rally at end of tumultuous week

organizations.name: bloomberg silicon valley high technology index

text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 9, 2018, 1:54pm PST Updated Feb 9, 2018, 2:01pm PST Silicon Valley stocks rebounded Friday, with the region's biggest tech companies all making gains at the end of one of the most volatile weeks in stock market history. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished Friday up 300 points, after convulsing through a 1,000-point range throughout the day. The Dow and the S&P 500 both ended the week down 5.2 percent — their worst performance in more than two years, CNBC noted . Silicon Valley stocks were led by chipmaker Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA), which Thursday reported better-than-expected earnings fueled by higher sales of its gaming and server chips. Its shares closed up 6.69 percent on Friday. The stock is one of Silicon Valley's best-performing, having gained more than 85 percent over the past 12 months. Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) closed up 5.09 percent, making it the best performer on the Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Technology Index , an index of the region’s 13 largest technology stocks. Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) followed, up 3.83 percent. Juniper Networks (NYSE: JNPR) gained 3.16 percent, Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC) rose 2.81 percent and Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) jumped 2.64 percent. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) bounced 1.22 percent. The worst performer on the index was Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), although the company still inched up 0.8 percent. Most of the stocks on the Bloomberg index slipped into correction territory this week , meaning they were down more than 10 percent from a recent high. The stock market turmoil kicked off last Friday as reports of continued wage and job growth in the U.S. sparked fears of rising inflation and interest rates. "What's happened here is an understanding that inflation is returning and that the central bank quantitative easing that we've grown accustomed to is coming to an end," Jim Bianco , head of the Chicago-based advisory firm Bianco Research, told CNBC . "Since the financial crisis, this is the first 10 percent correction in stocks that has not been accompanied by a significant fall in rates." – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 9, 2018, 1:54pm PST Updated Feb 9, 2018, 2:01pm PST Related Content
